_about: Public-domain Daniel Merrill (1765-1833), Congregational minister of Sedgwick, Maine, who became a Baptist with most of his church in 1805 and later served at Nottingham West, New Hampshire, for the Word Hoard: Open Communion, Twelve Letters to Samuel Austin, The Mode and Subjects of Baptism, Balaam Disappointed, and The Gospel Church Vindicated. Texts are from Internet Archive scans. Added 2026-10-23 by lane A, round 106 (my pick); Adam may veto the whole shelf. Every printing dated before 1930, so public domain in the US. No uids minted.

dmerrill-open-communion: Open communion with all who keep the ordinances as Christ delivered them to the saints : eight letters on open communion, addressed to Rufus Anderson (Boston : Printed and sold by Manning & Loring, 1805)
dmerrill-letters-austin: Twelve letters addressed to Rev. Samuel Austin, A.M. : in which his vindication of partial washing for Christian baptism, contained in ten letters, is reviewed and disproved (Boston : Printed by Manning & Loring, 1806)
dmerrill-baptism: The mode and subjects of baptism examined in seven sermons ([n.p.], 1812)
dmerrill-balaam: Balaam disappointed. A thanksgiving sermon, delivered at Nottingham-West, April 13, 1815. A day recommended by the national government, in which to rehearse God's mighty acts, and praise his name (Concord [N.H.] : Printed by Isaac & W.R. Hill, 1815)
dmerrill-gospel-church: The gospel church vindicated by the Scriptures (Concord : Printed by Hill & Moore, 1819)

_excluded.dmerrill-lee: A Thorough Method with Mr. Peter Edwards (by another hand)
